summary.text: Son whom Heracles begot on Omphale queen of Lydia during his servitude at her court — from Agelaus the Lydian house of Croesus was descended, though Croesus himself lies outside the seven atlas lenses.

story.text: When the Delphic oracle sold Heracles into bondage, Omphale daughter of Iardanes bought him and he served her as a slave in Lydia. Apollodorus counts among Heracles' many children by Omphale a son Agelaus, from whom the family of Croesus was descended — the genealogical bridge between the hero's Lydian sojourn and later Lydian kingship.
